body:
### Describe the bug

Since 3.2.0, unpacking a slice whose start is not a compile-time constant crashes the compiler in `MarkParallelAssignments`: `a, b = s[i:]`, `a, b = s[i:j]`, or the sliding-window idiom `a, b = values[i:i + 2]`. This is plain Python and the module does not build at all. 3.1.x compiles it and the result is correct.

The crash does not depend on the type of the sliced object or where the statement is:

- untyped, `list`, `str`, `bytes`, `tuple` and `tuple[int, str, float]` arguments, a local list, a method call result (`line.split()[i:]`) or an attribute (`o.items[i:]`)
- function, module level and class body; also a `.pyx` with `def f(list s, Py_ssize_t i)` and `@cython.compile`
- starred and nested targets: `a, *rest = s[i:]`, `*init, last = s[i:]`, `(a, b), c = s[i:]`, `[a, b] = s[i:]`, `x = a, b = s[i:]`
- also with `# cython: infer_types=False`

These compile: a constant start (`s[1:]`, `s[-2:]`, `s[1:j]`), no start (`s[:j]`), a slice with a step (`s[i::k]`), `t = s[i:]; a, b = t`, and `for a, b in pairs[i:]`.

### Code to reproduce the behaviour:

```python
# unpack.py
def first_two(s, i):
    a, b = s[i:]
    return a, b

print(first_two([1, 2, 3], 1))
```

`cython -3 unpack.py` (or `cythonize -i -3 unpack.py`):

```
Error compiling Cython file:
------------------------------------------------------------
...
def first_two(s, i):
    a, b = s[i:]
           ^
------------------------------------------------------------
unpack.py:2:11: Compiler crash in MarkParallelAssignments

ModuleNode.body = StatListNode(unpack.py:1:0)
StatListNode.stats[0] = DefNode(unpack.py:1:0, ...)
DefNode.body = StatListNode(unpack.py:2:4,
    is_terminator = True)
StatListNode.stats[0] = SingleAssignmentNode(unpack.py:2:12)
File 'ExprNodes.py', line 5676, in inferable_item_node: SliceIndexNode(unpack.py:2:12, ...)
File 'ExprNodes.py', line 755, in inferable_item_node: NameNode(unpack.py:2:11, name = 's', ...)

Compiler crash traceback from this point on:
  File ".../Cython/Compiler/ExprNodes.py", line 755, in inferable_item_node
    return IndexNode(self.pos, base=self, index=IntNode.for_size(self.pos, index))
                                                ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File ".../Cython/Compiler/ExprNodes.py", line 1575, in for_size
    return cls.for_int(pos, int_value, type=PyrexTypes.c_py_ssize_t_type)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File ".../Cython/Compiler/ExprNodes.py", line 1570, in for_int
    assert isinstance(int_value, int), repr(int_value)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
AssertionError: <NOT CONSTANT>
```

| | `cython -3 unpack.py` | `import unpack` |
|---|---|---|
| CPython 3.12.13 (not compiled) | | `(2, 3)` |
| Cython 3.0.12, 3.1.8 | compiles | `(2, 3)` |
| Cython 3.2.0, 3.2.9, 3.3.0, 3.3.1, master (211d68e) | **Compiler crash in MarkParallelAssignments** | |

### Expected behaviour

The module compiles, as with 3.1.x, and prints `(2, 3)`.

### OS

macOS 26.5 (ARM64)

### Python version

3.12.13

### Cython version

3.3.1 and master 211d68e (3.4.0a0); every version since 3.2.0

### Additional context

When the slice start is not constant, `SliceIndexNode.inferable_item_node()` passes `not_a_constant` on as the index ([ExprNodes.py#L5669-L5676](https://github.com/cython/cython/blob/211d68e592b5723de601620b02fc5bd914a2dd01/Cython/Compiler/ExprNodes.py#L5669-L5676)). `ExprNode.inferable_item_node()` passes that to `IntNode.for_size()` ([ExprNodes.py#L750-L755](https://github.com/cython/cython/blob/211d68e592b5723de601620b02fc5bd914a2dd01/Cython/Compiler/ExprNodes.py#L750-L755)), and `for_int()` asserts that the value is an `int` ([ExprNodes.py#L1568-L1575](https://github.com/cython/cython/blob/211d68e592b5723de601620b02fc5bd914a2dd01/Cython/Compiler/ExprNodes.py#L1568-L1575)). Up to 3.1.x, `inferable_item_node()` built the `IntNode` directly (`IntNode(self.pos, value=str(index), constant_result=index, type=PyrexTypes.c_py_ssize_t_type)`), which accepted `not_a_constant`. That line was changed to `IntNode.for_size()` in a2a713e (GH-7018), which is in 3.2.0.

Keeping the old construction for the `not_a_constant` case fixed it in my local test:

```diff
--- a/Cython/Compiler/ExprNodes.py
+++ b/Cython/Compiler/ExprNodes.py
@@ -752,7 +752,12 @@
         Return a node that represents the (type) result of an indexing operation,
         e.g. for tuple unpacking or iteration.
         """
-        return IndexNode(self.pos, base=self, index=IntNode.for_size(self.pos, index))
+        if index is not_a_constant:
+            index_node = IntNode(self.pos, value=str(index), constant_result=index,
+                                 type=PyrexTypes.c_py_ssize_t_type)
+        else:
+            index_node = IntNode.for_size(self.pos, index)
+        return IndexNode(self.pos, base=self, index=index_node)
```

With this change, all of the forms listed above compile, and the ones I ran give the same results as CPython (`first_two`, the sliding window, `tuple[int, str, float]`, the starred targets). `runtests.py` for `type_inference`, `arrayassign`, `tuple_unpack`, `unpack`, `ctuple` and `slice` still passes. I'm not sure it is the preferred fix; the type inference for these forms then works the same way as in 3.1.x.

I couldn't find a test with a non-constant start: `tests/run/arrayassign.pyx` only has constant slices (`x, y, z = a[1:4]`).
title: [BUG] 3.2 regression: compiler crash (AssertionError: <NOT CONSTANT>) on tuple unpacking of a slice with a variable start, `a, b = s[i:]`
